RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the March  2, 2006/Phalguna 11, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; External Affairs; Non-
Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning;
Power; Science and Technology; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Space; Statistics and Programme Implementation; Urban Development;
Urban Employment and Poverty Alleviation; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
Collapse of newly built highways in
Eastern India
*161. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are seized of
the incidents of portions of newly-built
highways under the Golden Quadrilateral
Project (GQP) caving in certain parts of
eastern India, in particular;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that NHAI has
adopted uniform technical parameters for
laying roads under the GQP throughout
the country in disregard to the varied
geological formations and soil texture
prevailing in different parts;
(d) if so, the rationale therefor;
(e) whether any investigation into the
reasons for collapse of sections of GQP
highways have been carried out and
accountability fixed; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Setting up of Indian Maritime Service
Cadre
*162. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any efforts have so far been
made to set up an Indian Maritime Service
Cadre;
(b) whether such a move will efficiently
serve the requirements of all maritime
related positions like shipping, light houses,
sea ports, vessels, etc.; and
(c) whether Government are considering
a proposal from Indian Maritime Industry
to employ foreign officers on case to case
basis if Indian hands are not available for
such positions?

52
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Repayment of loans to Asian
Development Bank
*163. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
SHRI AJAY MAROO:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National
Highway Authority of India has defaulted
in repayment of loans to the Asian
Development Bank;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the action taken/proposed to be
taken against the officers responsible for
this lapse?
Implementation of Central Right to
Information Act
*164. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have ensured
that the Central Right to Information Act is
being implemented throughout the country;
(b) whether any States are lagging
behind; and
(c) if so, which are these States and what
steps are being taken to ask those States
for its immediate implementation?
Revival of certain printing presses
†*165. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that printing
presses at Kolkata, Shimla, Chandigarh,
Gangtok and Stationery Office and Central
Farms Centres at Kolkata are without work
for the last many years;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the efforts being made by
Government to revive them?
Criticism of Power Incentive Scheme
*166.SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS KAUR:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Planning Commission
had criticized the Power Incentive Scheme,
insofar as it did not benefit the consumer
but the importer of power equipments/
appliances only, by way of reduction in
customs tariff; and
(b) if so, Government's response thereto
by way of reviewing and revising the
power policy so as to benefit the consumer,
directly?
Completion of Golden Quadrilateral
Scheme
†*167. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI  SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Golden Quadrilateral
Scheme for National Highways would be
completed within the stipulated time;
(b) if not, the reasons for the delay;
(c) whether Government propose to
award incentive to those who complete road
projects within time and penalize those who
delay completion thereof; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

53
Administrative Reforms Commission
†*168. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Administrative Reforms
Commission constituted by Government
has started functioning;
(b) if not, the handicaps it is facing; and
(c) if so, by when this Commission is
likely to submit its report to Government?

Total number of questions — 155
Intimation of policy decisions and
programmes to PMO
1019. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the practice, convention and
rules of our Cabinet system of governance
imply, inter-alia that policy decisions and
programmes, when framed by Ministries
and Departments, are intimated to the
Prime Minister's Office (PMO) well before
their introductions;
(b) whether the same is being done
away with;
(c) if so, the rationale thereof; and
(d) if not the veracity of recent news-
paper reports in the Press suggesting that
PMO has been writing since 3rd September,
2004 repeatedly to various Ministries/
Departments highlighting the growing
practice of informing the PMO of policy
decisions at the last moments only before
their scheduled official announcements?
Fire in collieries
†1020. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that several
collieries in the country are out of
production due to constant fire raging in
these collieries;
(b) if so, the locations of these collieries;
(c) the quantum of coal reserves
expected to be found in these collieries;
and
(d) the average quantity of coal
destroyed annually due to fire in the
collieries?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

232
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Commercial exploitation of coal by
private parties
1021. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
allow commercial exploitation of coal mines
by private parties;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government propose to
permit FDI in commercial exploitation of
coal?
Coal handling plant
†1022. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal to instal
a coal handling plant in the Northern
Coalfields Limited, Singrauli with a cost of
Rs. 173 crores;
(b) whether  Ranchi based Heavy
Engineering Corporation (HEC) has shown
any interest in the installation of this plant;
and
(c) if so, the details of the obstacles in
entrusting the work to the HEC?
Coal royalty to Jharkhand
†1023. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether at a meeting with the Prime
Minister, the Chief Minister of Jharkhand
has sought to increase royalty on coal to
the State to 20 per cent;
(b) whether such requests have also been
made by other States also; and
(c) Government's is view in this regard?
Right of coal mining
†1024. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are
contemplating on extending the right of
mining of coal from coal mines  facing
closure to cooperative society;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the total number of coal mines facing
closure at present; and
(d) whether Government are
contemplating on formulating a national
policy for the employees displaced from
the same in this regard?
Coal reserves under
BCCL
†1025. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is 4.6
billion tonnes of coal reserves under the
jurisdiction of Bharat Coking Coal Limited
where mining work is not going on at
present;
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) the total area of land where these
coal reserves exist;
(d) whether Government have recently
formulated any scheme for undertaking
mining work with regard to these reserves;
and
(e) if so, the details of this scheme?

233
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Passport office in Shimla
†1026. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the States that do not have any
passport office till yet;
(b) whether passport office has not been
established in Shimla, the capital of
Himachal Pradesh, so far;
(c) if so, the  reasons therefor; and
(d) by when a passport office would be
set up in the State capital to save the people
from the difficulties of going to Chandigarh
and to make passport expeditiously?
